title: Evaluator core (eval/apply)
description: Implement the eval/apply loop over datums. Dispatch on form: self-evaluating, variable reference, special-form lookup, procedure application. Apply handles both primitive and closure procedures. This is the spine; special forms and built-ins plug into it. Tail calls handled by trampolining (proper TCO is a separate later bead but design should leave room).
design:
Evaluator is an explicit step-loop, NOT recursive Rust calls. Shape:

  loop {
      match state {
          Step::Eval(expr, env) => ...,    // -> Step::Apply | Step::Tail | Step::Done
          Step::Apply(proc, args) => ...,  // -> Step::Eval | Step::Done
          Step::Tail(expr, env) => continue, // tail call: no Rust stack growth
          Step::Done(v) => return v,
      }
  }

A continuation is a Vec<Frame> describing pending work. Push a frame when entering a non-tail subexpression; pop when its value is ready. This makes:
  - TCO (T11): free — tail calls reuse the current frame instead of pushing
  - call/cc (T17): clone() the frame vector to capture a continuation; replace the vector to invoke
  - Exception handling (T18): unwind frames searching for a handler

Why: writing eval as recursive Rust calls forces a rewrite for both TCO and call/cc. Bake the shape now; the user-facing call/cc procedure can still ship in T17.
notes:
Implemented in src/eval.rs (~830 lines incl. 28 inline tests) plus tests/eval.rs (6 integration tests).

Implements the architecture from docs/0001-tree-walking-interpreter.md:

- Step enum: Eval(Value, EnvRef), Apply(Value, Vec<Value>), Return(Value)
- Frame enum: IfBranch, BeginRest, DefineBind, SetBind, CallOp, CallArg
- Frames own their state by value (Vec<Frame> is clone-able for T17 call/cc)
- The eval() function is an explicit loop over Step, NOT recursive Rust calls

Tail-position discipline (verified by deep-recursion tests):
- Frame::IfBranch.resume() transitions Step::Eval(chosen_branch, env) WITHOUT pushing a frame
- Frame::BeginRest.resume() — when only the last expression remains, transitions Step::Eval without re-pushing
- Frame::CallArg.resume() — when remaining is empty, transitions Step::Apply (no frame pushed); Apply for closure transitions to eval_sequence over the body
- eval_sequence places only the last expression at tail position

Special forms implemented here (per advisor's T7/T8 split):
- quote: takes one operand, returns it unevaluated
- if: 2 or 3 operands; pushes IfBranch frame; alt is optional (#f case returns Unspecified)
- lambda: parses formals (fixed, dotted, rest-symbol, empty); builds Procedure::Closure
- define: bare form (define name value); shorthand (define (name . formals) body...) constructs and binds a named closure
- set!: walks env to find existing binding; errors otherwise
- begin: evaluates each expression in sequence; returns last; (begin) returns Unspecified

Procedure application:
- step_apply checks arity (Primitive uses Arity enum; Closure checks fixed vs rest)
- Closure body uses eval_sequence with last in tail position
- Calling a non-procedure raises RuntimeError::NotProcedure
- Closures share their EnvRef via Rc clone — mutual recursion works (integration test confirms)

Convenience APIs:
- pub fn eval(expr: Value, env: EnvRef) -> Result<Value, EvalError>
- pub fn eval_source(source: &str, env: EnvRef) — full lex+parse+eval

EvalError wraps RuntimeError, ParseError, plus MalformedForm for special-form arity / shape errors.

Tail-recursion smoke tests:
- (loop n) with n=100k via tail-call: passes, stack stays O(1)
- Tail position inside (begin) and nested (if): passes
- Integration test (tests/eval.rs) confirms lex→parse→eval seam at n=100k

Closure variant added to Procedure (in value.rs). EnvRef imported into value.rs — modules cross-reference but no circular types thanks to Rc.

Deferred to T8 (nscheme-i4h): let, let*, letrec, letrec*, let-values, let*-values, cond (with => clauses), case, and, or, when, unless, do, delay, parameterize, quasiquote expansion.

title: Environment and lexical scoping
description: Implement the Environment type: nested frames, lexical lookup, define/set! semantics (define adds to current frame, set! mutates existing binding or errors), shared parent references for closures. Must support efficient lookup and the mutation rules R7RS requires.
notes:
Implemented in src/env.rs (~210 lines incl. 10 tests).

Env = single frame (RefCell<HashMap<Symbol, Value>>) + Option<Rc<Env>> parent.
EnvRef = Rc<Env>; closures capture by cloning EnvRef so multiple captures over the same scope all observe each other's mutations (needed for letrec, mutual recursion).

Semantics:
- define(name, value): bind in current frame; replace if name already bound here. Does NOT walk up.
- lookup(name): walk parent chain, return first hit.
- set(name, value): walk parent chain to find the nearest enclosing binding; mutate in place. Errors with RuntimeError::Undefined if no binding anywhere.

Tested:
- Defined lookup; missing returns None
- Parent inheritance; child shadowing without affecting parent
- set! mutates current frame
- set! walks to parent frame (and changes are visible to parent and siblings)
- set! on undefined symbol returns Undefined error
- set! prefers nearest (child) binding over global
- Shared frames seen by multiple captures
- local_len counts current frame only
close_reason: Environment complete; 10 tests pass.

title: Core runtime value types
description: Define the Value enum / runtime representation: pair, null, symbol (interned), number (initially fixnum + f64; full tower in later bead), char, string, vector, bytevector, boolean, procedure (primitive + closure), port (stub), eof-object, unspecified. Choose between Rc<RefCell> vs arena vs Gc<T> for cyclic structures — document the choice. Implement eqv?/equal?/eq? semantics.
design:
Cycle handling: use Rc<RefCell<...>> for mutable cells (pairs, vectors, strings, boxes). Document the leak: cyclic structures created via set-car!/set-cdr! will NOT be reclaimed until process exit. This is acceptable for v1 — most amateur Scheme interpreters do this. A proper GC (gc crate or custom mark-sweep) is deferred future work, not in scope for the epic.

Value enum sketch (subject to refinement in implementation):
  Value::Null
  Value::Bool(bool)
  Value::Char(char)
  Value::Symbol(Symbol)            // interned string id
  Value::Int(i64)                  // fast path for fixnums
  Value::BigInt(Rc<BigInt>)        // exact integer overflow
  Value::Rational(Rc<BigRational>) // exact rational
  Value::Float(f64)                // inexact real
  Value::String(Rc<RefCell<String>>)
  Value::Pair(Rc<RefCell<Pair>>)
  Value::Vector(Rc<RefCell<Vec<Value>>>)
  Value::Bytevector(Rc<RefCell<Vec<u8>>>)
  Value::Procedure(Rc<Procedure>)
  Value::Port(Rc<RefCell<Port>>)
  Value::Eof
  Value::Unspecified

Equality:
  eq?: pointer/identity equality for heap values; value equality for atoms
  eqv?: like eq? but with sane number comparison across exact/inexact
  equal?: structural (recurses pairs/vectors/strings)
notes:
Implemented in src/value.rs (~800 lines incl. 23 inline tests).

Surface:
- Value enum: Null, Unspecified, Eof, Bool, Char, Symbol, Int(i64), Float(f64), String, Pair, Vector, Bytevector, Procedure, Port
- Symbol: interned via thread-local RefCell<HashMap<String, Rc<str>>>; equality by Rc pointer; Hash by pointer-as-usize
- Pair { car, cdr } wrapped in Rc<RefCell<>>
- Procedure enum (Primitive variant only; Closure added in T7)
- PrimitiveFn = fn(&[Value]) -> Result<Value>
- Arity { Exact(n), AtLeast(n), Range { min, max } } with matches() helper
- Port: stubbed for T14 to populate
- RuntimeError (thiserror): Type, Arity, Undefined, NotProcedure, DivisionByZero, Other

R7RS equality:
- eq(): identity equality (pointer for heap, value for atoms)
- eqv(): like eq, distinguishes numeric exactness (will be refined when T12 adds BigInt/Rational)
- equal(): structural recurse; uses a visited HashSet keyed by Rc::as_ptr to terminate on cyclic input (R7RS §6.1)

Display/Debug:
- Debug uses R7RS 'write' (escapes in strings, #\name for special chars)
- Display uses R7RS 'display' (raw characters and string contents)
- Special-cased: floats render with a trailing .0 (or +inf.0, -inf.0, +nan.0) so the reader round-trips them as inexact
- Lists print canonically including dotted-pair improper lists

Helpers:
- Value::cons, list_from, string, vector, bytevector constructors
- is_null/is_pair/is_boolean/is_symbol/is_number/is_string/is_vector/is_procedure
- is_truthy (R7RS: everything but #f is true)
- list_length using Floyd's tortoise-and-hare for cycle detection
- as_pair() destructure
- type_name() for error messages

Deferred:
- BigInt, BigRational variants (T12 numeric tower)
- Procedure::Closure variant (T7 evaluator)
- Port internals (T14 I/O)

title: Parser: tokens to datum/AST
description: Build a recursive-descent (or equivalent) parser that turns the token stream into Scheme datums. Handle proper and improper lists, vectors, bytevectors, quote-family reader macros, and produce structured parse errors with source spans. Output is a Datum tree consumable by the evaluator (not a separate IR — Scheme programs are themselves datums).
notes:
Implemented in src/parse.rs (~470 lines incl. 27 inline tests).

Parser is a thin recursive descent over the Token stream, producing runtime Value directly (Scheme programs are data).

Handled:
- Atoms: Boolean, Character, String, Identifier (interned to Symbol), Number (Int/Float in v1)
- Lists: proper (a b c) → Pair chain, improper (a b . c) → terminating pair, () → Null
- Vectors #(...), bytevectors #u8(...) with element-range check (0..=255)
- Reader macros 'x → (quote x), `x → (quasiquote x), ,x → (unquote x), ,@x → (unquote-splicing x)
- Datum comments #; skip exactly one following datum, both top-level and inside lists/vectors
- Errors: UnexpectedEof, UnexpectedRParen, UnexpectedDot, UnclosedList, BadDottedTail, InvalidNumber, BadBytevectorElement, Lex (forwarded LexError)

Numeric subset for v1 (the numeric tower bead nscheme-c92 will broaden):
- Decimal/radix integers parsed to i64; overflow returns InvalidNumber rather than wrapping
- Decimals/exponents parsed to f64
- +inf.0, -inf.0, +nan.0 recognized
- Rationals (a/b) and complex (a+bi, a@b) lexically rejected — they parse as a number lexeme but the converter returns InvalidNumber

Public API: parse_program (full source → Vec<Value>) and parse_one (exactly one datum).

Added Clone derive to LexError so it can be wrapped via #[from] in ParseError.
close_reason: Parser complete; 27 tests pass.

title: Lexer / tokenizer
description: Tokenize Scheme source text into tokens: identifiers, numbers (with R7RS lexical syntax including #e/#i/#b/#o/#d/#x prefixes), booleans (#t/#f/#true/#false), characters (#\name and #\x...), strings (with escapes), parens, dot, quote/quasiquote/unquote/unquote-splicing reader macros, vector prefix #(, bytevector prefix #u8(, comments (line ;, block #| |#, datum #;). Span/position tracking for error messages.
notes:
Implemented in src/lex.rs (~700 lines incl. 37 inline tests).

Token kinds covered:
- LParen, RParen, VectorStart (#(), BytevectorStart (#u8(), Dot
- Quote, Quasiquote, Unquote, UnquoteSplicing, DatumComment (#;)
- Boolean (short #t/#f and long #true/#false forms)
- Number(NumberLexeme) carrying radix (2/8/10/16) + exactness (#e/#i) + raw body; prefixes can be in either order
- Character: single-char #\x, named #\newline/space/tab/null/return/escape/delete/alarm/backspace, hex #\xHEX
- String with escapes (\a \b \t \n \r \" \\ \| \xHEX;) and line continuations
- Identifier: simple, |...|-quoted with escapes, peculiar (+, -, ..., ->foo)

Comments: ; line, #| ... |# block (nests properly), #; datum (emitted as a marker token for the parser to elide).

Edge cases verified by tests:
- #trues lexes as #t followed by identifier 'rues' (boolean short-form delimiter rule)
- #e#xFF and #x#eFF both lex to radix=16 exact (R7RS prefix-order flexibility)
- +inf.0 / -inf.0 / +nan.0 / -nan.0 lex as numbers, not identifiers
- ... lexes as identifier, standalone . lexes as Dot
- Nested block comments
- Spans match source positions

Numeric values are NOT parsed here — Number tokens carry raw bodies and the numeric tower (T12) does the structured parsing. This keeps the lexer simple and decouples lexical recognition from numeric semantics.

title: Teaching-quality refactor: in-code commentary + guided tour
description:
# Goal

Convert nscheme into a teaching-quality codebase: 100% behavior preserved, all tests still pass, but every file is written and annotated as if it were a chapter in a book aimed at strong professional programmers who are new to *both* Rust and Scheme.

# Scope

## What changes

- Every src/*.rs file gets a teaching-comment pass:
  - File header (//!) explaining what concepts this file teaches and what to read alongside it.
  - Section comments grouping related code.
  - First-appearance idiom notes: explain Rc<RefCell<…>>, lifetimes, ? chains, exhaustive match, thiserror, etc. *the first time they appear* (and only then).
  - Scheme-concept notes: quasiquote, hygiene, continuations, the numeric tower, exact vs inexact, tail position — explain when first encountered.
  - Cross-references to ADRs (docs/0001..0006) and R7RS section numbers.
- One structural split: src/eval.rs (3643 lines) becomes the step loop + a sibling module for the Frame catalog + a sibling module for per-special-form dispatch. Done as part of the sweep, not before.
- New: docs/STYLE.md — distilled style guide produced in phase 1, signed off before the sweep.
- New: TOUR.md at repo root — guided tour with overview architecture, suggested reading orders, per-module pointers, cross-references to ADRs and PROJECT.md.
- Minor: README.md gets a pointer to TOUR.md; docs/README.md index updated.

## What does NOT change

- Public API and behavior. cargo test stays green. Chibi conformance stays 1225/1225.
- Third-party vendored corpus (tests/r7rs-corpus/).
- The 7 ADRs (docs/0001-0006) — historical record; the guide REFERENCES them.
- PROJECT.md (retrospective — separate artifact).
- CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md (managed by bd init).
- The bead database itself.

# Phases

1. Style guide. Apply the teaching-comment style to value.rs and a slice of eval.rs as the prototype. Distill into docs/STYLE.md. STOP for sign-off.
2. Sweep. Apply the style to every other src file in module-graph order, splitting eval.rs along the way.
3. TOUR.md. Top-level reading guide.
4. Verify. Full lint + tests + conformance.

# Design decisions (recorded for context)

- Audience: strong programmer, new to Rust *and* Scheme. Idiomatic Rust is the target; the comments explain idioms on first appearance only.
- TOUR.md lives at repo root (discoverable; renders prominently on GitHub).
- docs/STYLE.md lives in docs/ (sits with the ADRs).
- 'Try this' exercises are deferred — separate follow-up bead AFTER this work lands. The author wants to see what I have in mind before committing.
- builtins.rs and value.rs stay as single files. builtins is a flat catalog (right pattern for that). value.rs at ~1800 lines is borderline but still coherent.
- eval.rs IS split — three concerns (step loop, Frame catalog, special-form dispatch) are naturally separable and the file's length is currently the main impediment to reading it.
- The 7 ADRs are not rewritten — they're a record of *past* decision-making and stand as primary sources that the guide cites.
- PROJECT.md is the retrospective and is left untouched.

title: Library loader: find / load (lib) from filesystem search path
description:
## Gap
We have define-library and a thread-local registry, but no way to LOAD a library from a file. \`(import (foo bar))\` only resolves to:
1. The hard-coded builtin list in src/library.rs (\`(scheme base)\`, etc.).
2. Whatever the running program has registered via earlier \`(define-library …)\` forms in the same session.

There's no file-system search: nscheme can't find \`foo/bar.sld\` or \`foo/bar.scm\` on a path like SCHEME_LOAD_PATH.

## When it matters
Adopting any third-party R7RS library — including R7RS-large reference implementations — without copy-pasting source into the program.

## Suggested fix
1. Add SCHEME_LOAD_PATH-style env var + a built-in default (e.g., ./lib/, \$XDG_DATA_HOME/nscheme/lib).
2. When import_one encounters an unknown library name, search the path for matching .sld / .scm files, load with eval_source in a sandboxed env, then proceed.
3. Cache by library name so repeated imports don't re-parse.
4. ADR to document the search algorithm.

Blocked-by: library imports share cells (so loaded libraries' mutable bindings work).

title: Import set qualifiers: only / except / rename / prefix
description:
## Gap
R7RS §5.6.1 defines import-set qualifiers:
- (only (lib) name1 name2 …)
- (except (lib) name1 name2 …)
- (prefix (lib) prefix:)
- (rename (lib) (orig new) …)

Our \`step_import\` calls \`crate::library::parse_library_name(lib_form)\` and then bulk-installs every export. The qualifier forms above either fail to parse as a library name or silently import everything.

## When it matters
Code that imports just one or two names from a larger library, or renames to avoid clashes. Common pattern when mixing libraries that share names (e.g., scheme/list vs. srfi/1).

## Suggested fix
1. Recognise (only …) / (except …) / (prefix …) / (rename …) as the FORM, not the name.
2. Resolve the inner import-set to a {name -> Value} map, then filter/rename/prefix before defining in the target env.
3. Allow nested qualifiers.
4. Add tests covering each form.

title: Reader audit: block comments, datum-label edge cases, R6RS-compat directives
description:
## Gap
The chibi corpus exercises most reader syntax but not every R7RS lexical form. We haven't separately confirmed:
- Block comments \`#| ... |#\` (and nested block comments per R7RS §7.1.1).
- \`#!fold-case\` / \`#!no-fold-case\` per-port state (we keep one flag on the parser; multiple reads on the same port should preserve it across calls).
- Datum labels spanning multiple top-level (read) calls.
- \`#!r6rs\` directive (R6RS compat — not required by R7RS, but some Schemes accept).
- \`#:keyword\` or other extension syntax some Schemes accept.
- Very long datum labels (#999999=) and very deeply nested.
- Characters: every R7RS-named char (alarm, backspace, delete, escape, newline, null, return, space, tab) plus \`#\\xHEX\` for arbitrary scalars.

## When it matters

## Suggested fix
1. Write a test exercising every R7RS §7.1.1 production.
2. Implement / fix any that don't work.
3. Add an ADR documenting which non-standard lexical extensions, if any, we accept.

title: R7RS-small library completeness audit
description:
## Gap

## Suggested fix
1. Walk R7RS-small §6 and §B (the library list). For each procedure, confirm it's defined and behaves per spec.
2. File a sub-bead for any procedure that's missing or stubbed.
3. Add targeted unit tests for the procedures the chibi corpus doesn't exercise.

title: Audit tail-call positions per R7RS §3.5
description:
## Gap
We have a step-loop evaluator with a Vec<Frame> stack — tail calls don't grow the host Rust stack. But we haven't verified that every R7RS-mandated tail position actually reuses the current frame (vs pushing a new one).

R7RS §3.5 lists the tail positions:
- The body of a procedure call (the last expression)
- The conseq and alt of \`if\`
- Each clause body of \`cond\`, \`case\`, \`when\`, \`unless\`
- The last expression of \`and\` / \`or\` / \`begin\`
- The body of \`let\`, \`let*\`, \`letrec\`, \`letrec*\`, \`let-syntax\`, \`letrec-syntax\`, \`let-values\`, \`let*-values\`, \`parameterize\`, \`guard\`, \`when\`, \`unless\`
- The thunk passed to \`dynamic-wind\` (its return propagates through)
- The expression in \`(if test conseq)\` with no \`alt\`

## When it matters
Deeply recursive programs (mutual recursion, state machines, parser combinators) — should run in constant frame stack depth.

## Suggested fix
1. Read each step_* in eval.rs against R7RS §3.5 and confirm the tail expression doesn't push a frame.
2. Add a stress test: a function that does 1_000_000 tail-recursive calls in each form. Run with a small stack to catch leaks.
3. Document the audit in a new ADR or extend ADR 0001.

title: Library imports copy values; should share mutable cells
description:
## Gap
\`(import (lib))\` calls Env::define(name, value) for each exported binding — value, not a shared cell. So:
  - set! on an imported variable inside the importer's scope doesn't propagate to the library's binding.
  - set! inside the library after the import doesn't propagate to importers.
Currently we work around this in the chibi-test-shim by *not* using define-library: the shim is loaded directly into the test env so its set!s on \$passes / \$fails hit the same binding the test runner reads.

## When it matters
Any library that exposes mutable state: counters, registries, plugin tables, on-load hooks. R7RS \`(define foo 0)\` + \`(define (bump!) (set! foo (+ foo 1)))\` exported from a library should let importers see the increment.

## Suggested fix
Change Env's frame to HashMap<Symbol, Rc<RefCell<Value>>>:
- lookup returns the cell's borrowed value.
- set!/define mutate / create the cell.
- import_one binds the cell directly (target.bind_cell(name, source.cell(name))).
Touches every lookup/set call site but is a self-contained refactor.

A lighter alternative: leave Env as-is for normal use; only for library imports, insert a Value::Alias(Rc<RefCell<Value>>) that lookup/set/define dereference. Smaller blast radius but adds an indirection layer in lookups.

title: syntax-rules macros
description: Implement R7RS hygienic macros via syntax-rules: define-syntax let-syntax letrec-syntax, pattern matching with literals and ..., template expansion with hygiene (alpha-renaming of introduced identifiers). syntax-rules is the only macro system required by R7RS-small. syntax-case is NOT required and deferred.
notes:
Implemented src/macros.rs (~620 lines incl. tests). Approach: alpha-renaming (KFFD-style) hygiene per advisor.

Architecture:
- Added Value::Macro(Rc<SyntaxRules>) variant
- SyntaxRules = { literals: HashSet<Symbol>, clauses: Vec<SyntaxClause> }
- step_eval recognizes macro applications: when (head args...) and head resolves to Value::Macro, expand and emit Step::Eval(expanded, env) — re-evaluates the result so nested macros work
- define-syntax, let-syntax, letrec-syntax are special forms in eval.rs

Pattern matching:
- Symbol pattern (not literal, not _, not ...): binds to input value
- _ : wildcard, no binding
- Literal symbol: must match the same identifier in input
- (p ...): zero-or-more, collects per-rep bindings as Match::Multi
- Dotted-tail patterns: supported
- Improper-list inputs: walked

Template instantiation:
- Symbol in bindings → substitute value
- Symbol in rename map → renamed gensym
- p ...: looks up multi-binding for vars in p, splices

Hygiene via alpha-renaming:
- collect_binders walks the template, identifies identifiers in binding positions (lambda formals, let-binding names, define LHS, do bindings)
- Each such identifier (excluding pattern variables) gets a gensym: name#N
- These renames are applied uniformly when instantiating

Advisor's four failure-mode tests all pass:
- swap!: tmp doesn't capture user's tmp (hygiene)
- my-let*: ellipsis pattern and template, recursive expansion
- literals: 'then'/'else' as literal keywords don't bind arbitrary inputs
- (_ ...): _ is wildcard, not macro name

Plus tests for nested macro expansion (key spec requirement), let-syntax, and multi-clause selection.

Documented v1 limitations:
- Free identifiers in templates use the *call site's* env (not definition site). Most amateur Schemes have this — fixing requires syntactic closures or sets-of-scopes.
- Nested ellipsis depth >1 not supported
- Custom ellipsis identifier syntax not supported

Internal Num helper enum (Int|Float) handles exact→inexact promotion uniformly across arithmetic and comparison: any operation mixing Int and Float promotes to Float; integer division that doesn't divide evenly also promotes to Float (numeric-tower bead T12 will replace with exact rationals).

Modulo semantics: result has sign of divisor (R7RS). Quotient truncates toward zero. Remainder has sign of dividend. All three tested.

Scheme bootstrap (constant BOOTSTRAP, evaluated after Rust primitives):
- (define (map f xs) ...) — recursive, O(n) frame growth (R7RS doesn't mandate TCO for map)
- (define (for-each f xs) ...) — tail-recursive, runs at O(1) stack
- cxr shortcuts: caar cadr cdar cddr caddr cadddr

Verified: 24 tests pass including bootstrap-defined map/for-each, all predicate semantics, set-car!/set-cdr! mutation, mixed exact/inexact comparisons.

title: Core special forms
description: Implement R7RS-small special forms: quote, if, lambda, define, set!, begin, let, let*, letrec, letrec*, let-values, let*-values, cond (with => clauses), case, and, or, when, unless, do, delay, parameterize, quasiquote/unquote/unquote-splicing. Derived forms can be expressed in terms of core forms; document which are primitive vs derived.
notes:
Added 11 derived special forms to src/eval.rs (~600 lines added incl. 28 new tests).

Forms implemented:
- let, let* (desugared)
- letrec, letrec* (desugared to (let ((v <unspec>) ...) (set! v e) ... body); R7RS allows sequential evaluation for both — documented in the bead and code)
- named let (desugared to letrec-form per R7RS)
- when, unless (desugared via if; unless uses (if test #unspec body) where #unspec = (if #f #f))
- cond with single-test, body, and => clauses (test value held in Frame::CondArrow to avoid double evaluation)
- case with eqv? matching (NOT equal? — the common amateur mistake; verified by test)
- and, or with short-circuit AND last expression in tail position (Frame::AndNext / OrNext)
- do (desugared to letrec loop)
- quasiquote / unquote / unquote-splicing (single-level only — nested quasiquote deferred)

New Frame variants: CondClause, CondArrow, AndNext, OrNext. All variants own their state by value (cloning the Vec<Frame> for call/cc remains free).

Tail-position discipline maintained:
- cond body / else body / => apply: tail
- and/or last expression: tail (Frame not pushed for tail)
- when/unless body via if: tail (inherited from if's tail discipline)
- do: tail via letrec loop body

Filed follow-up beads (out of T8 scope, would expand Value enum mid-bead):
- nscheme-hs5: delay/force lazy promises (needs Value::Promise variant)
- nscheme-z5o: parameterize and make-parameter (needs Parameter variant)

title: Backtraces / source spans for raised exceptions
description:
## Gap
When a Scheme exception escapes uncaught, the error message identifies the type and the irritants but not WHERE the error occurred. Source-span tracking in the parser exists (every Value::Pair could carry a Span) but isn't threaded through evaluation.

## When it matters
Debugging user code. Particularly painful for syntax errors in macro-expanded forms — the user sees an error in a position that doesn't exist in their source.

## Suggested fix
1. Add an optional Rc<Span> next to each Value::Pair (or a sidecar HashMap<Rc-pointer, Span>).
2. Parser populates spans as it builds the AST.
3. Macro expander either preserves spans or attaches the call-site span as a fallback.
4. Step::Raise carries the span of the raise site (already partially possible via guard frames).
5. Uncaught raise error formats span:line:col → source line → caret.

Big change; do it after the simpler R7RS gaps are closed.

title: R7RS-large: Red Edition (2016) libraries
description:
## Gap
R7RS-large is the ongoing larger-language project (Working Group 2). Red Edition (ratified 2016) defines these libraries, none of which we implement:

- (scheme list)       — SRFI 1 list library
- (scheme charset)    — SRFI 14 character-sets
- (scheme hash-table) — SRFI 125 intermediate hash tables
- (scheme ileave)     — SRFI 134 immutable deques
- (scheme list-queue) — SRFI 117 mutable queues
- (scheme generator)  — SRFI 158 generators / accumulators
- (scheme lseq)       — SRFI 127 lazy sequences
- (scheme set)        — SRFI 113 sets and bags
- (scheme sort)       — SRFI 132 sort
- (scheme stream)     — SRFI 41 streams
- (scheme box)        — SRFI 111 boxes
- (scheme comparator) — SRFI 128 comparators
- (scheme regex)      — SRFI 115 regular expressions (some sources put this in Tangerine)

## When it matters
Any code targeting R7RS-large (a growing portion of new R7RS code).

## Suggested fix
Each library has a reference implementation linked from the SRFI document. Most are pure Scheme and would drop in once we either:
1. Have a working library system that can load .scm files from a search path, or
2. Inline the bootstrap source the way we do for current-input-port etc.

Prioritise the most-used ones first: scheme/list, scheme/hash-table, scheme/sort, scheme/comparator, scheme/box.

Make sure the underlying primitives each depends on are present (e.g., hash-table needs a record-based hash; sort needs a fast vector-sort primitive).
notes: DESIGN (2026-06-02, approved by author): Implementing full R7RS-large (Red+Tangerine) via on-disk .scm libraries + filesystem loader (chosen over include_str! vendoring). Decomposed into one child bead per SRFI library, dependency-ordered: comparator(128) first as it underpins set/hash-table/mapping; sort(132) needs vector-sort! primitive; hash-table(125) needs hash primitive. Per-library protocol: vendor SRFI reference .scm (license header preserved) into lib/ tree, wire missing primitives, port that SRFI's own test suite, cargo test green, one bead = one commit. Phase 0 prereqs (must precede libs): q1c shared-cells refactor, 9q5 loader, e0s import qualifiers, + Rust primitive beads.

title: User-defined error categories beyond read-error? / file-error?
description:
## Gap
ErrorObject carries a kind field with three variants: User, Read, File — used by error-object? / read-error? / file-error?. R7RS-small allows that, but real-world Scheme code wants to attach a TYPE TAG (\"my-app-not-found-error\", \"my-app-config-error\") so handlers can dispatch.

R7RS-large is likely to standardise an error-type / condition system. Many SRFIs (SRFI 35 conditions, SRFI 36 I/O conditions) already do.

## When it matters
Any user library wanting to throw typed errors and handle them by type instead of by parsing the message string.

## Suggested fix
Option A (minimal): add an optional Value tag to ErrorObject (\`tag: Option<Value>\`) plus \`make-error-object/tagged\` and \`error-object-tag\` accessor. Convention is that the tag is a symbol or record.

Option B (R7RS-large prep): implement SRFI 35 conditions on top of define-record-type. ErrorObject becomes a record with predicate chains.

Wait for the R7RS-large committee's decision before committing; option A is forward-compatible.

title: eval should be a first-class procedure
description:
## Gap
\`eval\` is currently a special form (step_eval matches \"eval\" by name and routes through step_eval_form). R7RS \`(scheme eval)\` specifies \`eval\` as a normal procedure that can be passed around and applied.

Symptoms today:
- \`(apply eval (list '(+ 1 2) (interaction-environment)))\` fails — apply can't take a special form as a procedure value.
- \`(map eval forms)\` fails for the same reason.
- \`(define run eval)\` then \`(run '(+ 1 2))\` fails — special-form dispatch happens by symbol-name lookup before env lookup.

## When it matters
Macros that build code and feed it through (map eval …); REPLs; embedding interpreters.

## Suggested fix
Add a Procedure::Eval variant (or a primitive that takes the eval logic). step_apply handles it by calling step_eval(expr, env) with the supplied arguments. Bind it under the symbol \`eval\` in the global env so symbol lookup finds the procedure.

Need to keep eval's tail-call property: the result of \`(eval expr env)\` is in tail position relative to the apply site. Push the right frame so the eval steps return to the caller's continuation.

title: Test shim uses approx-equal float compare; deviates from chibi's (chibi test)
description:
## Gap
tests/r7rs-corpus/chibi-test-shim.scm is OUR rewrite of (chibi test). It deviates from the upstream library in one material way:

  \$test-equal? compares numbers with ~1e-6 relative tolerance (plus a small absolute floor) instead of bit-exact equal?. NaN-vs-NaN counts as equal so the corpus's tests for nan? results work.

Without the relaxation ~15 corpus assertions would fail because the corpus pins float literals like \`20.0855369231877\` that don't bit-match libm's (exp 3) result.

Other deviations: the shim isn't wrapped in (define-library) — it's loaded directly into the test env to dodge the value-copying import issue (see separate bead).

## When it matters
Conformance reporting honesty. We claim "passes the chibi corpus" but with a relaxed comparison oracle.

## Suggested fix
Drop the float-tolerance once two upstream issues are resolved:
1. Library imports share cells (bead nscheme-XXX), so the shim can be wrapped in define-library like upstream.
2. Float printing matches chibi byte-for-byte (bead nscheme-XXX — adopt Ryu).

Then the shim can be a verbatim copy of chibi's (chibi test). The 15 currently-skirted assertions either pass (if our float printer now matches) or fail (in which case they're over-precise corpus bugs to file upstream).

title: Unicode case folding: extend beyond ad-hoc table
description:
## Gap
\`case_fold\` in src/builtins.rs handles the corpus-tested edge cases — ß → ss, ſ → s, ς → σ — on top of Rust's to_lowercase. The Unicode CaseFolding.txt has hundreds more entries (Turkish dotted/dotless i, Lithuanian special cases, Cherokee, Adlam, etc.) we don't cover.

## When it matters
\`string-foldcase\` / \`string-ci=?\` on non-Latin scripts in user code. R7RS §6.7 requires "full Unicode case folding" — our coverage is incomplete.

## Suggested fix
Add a Unicode-aware crate dependency:
- \`unicode-case-mapping\` — applies CaseFolding.txt's C (common), F (full), and S (simple) mappings.
- or \`caseless\` — already does R7RS-style foldcase.
Replace the hand-rolled case_fold with a call into the crate. Keep the small table as a fallback for the bytes-only path if we don't want a dependency.

title: Exact-complex arithmetic falls through to inexact
description:
## Gap
Value::Complex now stores arbitrary number Values per component (so the reader keeps \`1+2i\` exact and \`1.0+2i\` mixed-exact). But arithmetic on complex goes through Num::Complex(f64, f64): num_add / num_sub / num_mul / num_div all convert to f64.

  (+ 1+2i 3+4i)
    expected: exact 4+6i
    got:      inexact 4.0+6.0i

## When it matters
Exact symbolic arithmetic with complex inputs; tests that compare \`(make-rectangular 1 2)\` to \`(+ 0+i 1+2i -0-i)\` via \`equal?\`. R7RS §6.2 promises the exact tower stays exact if all inputs are exact, including for complex.

## Suggested fix
Add an exact-complex arithmetic path:
- num_add: if both Num::Complex components are exact (Int / BigInt / Rational), produce a Value::Complex with BigRational components.
- Same for sub / mul / div / neg.
- Promote to inexact only when an operand is itself inexact.

Cleanest implementation: factor a ComplexNum enum (Exact{re:BigRational, im:BigRational} | Inexact{re:f64, im:f64}) and route the four ops through it.

title: Float printing: prefer Ryu over custom 15-digit-then-widen
description:
## Gap
Our write_float tries 15 / 16 / 17 significant digits and picks the shortest that round-trips. The chibi-test-shim has to use approximate-equality for floats anyway, partly because some boundary values produce strings that differ from chibi's reference output by a digit.

## When it matters
Conformance tests that pin float literals tightly (the chibi corpus has ~15 such assertions). Real users typically don't care — both forms parse back to the same f64. But test corpus interop is the cleanest fix.

## Suggested fix
Pull in the \`ryu\` crate (the de facto Rust crate for shortest-round-trip f64 printing). Use ryu::Buffer::format(x) and post-process for Scheme syntax:
- Add a decimal point or exponent if the result is a plain integer (so it reads as inexact).
- +inf.0 / -inf.0 / +nan.0 for non-finite (already done).
- Match chibi's choice of fixed vs scientific notation by exponent range.

Then drop the chibi-test-shim's approximate-equality and re-run — any remaining failures are over-precise corpus expectations and should be filed upstream against chibi.

title: Macro hygiene: full sets-of-scopes
description:
## Gap
Our hygiene uses Value::SyntaxRef { name, env } as a coarse approximation of Racket-style sets-of-scopes. Pattern bindings are keyed by (name, env_ptr) so template-introduced and substituted identifiers are distinguished. Head dispatch tries def-env, then special-form name, then call-site env (so let-syntax bindings inside a template stay visible).

This passes the chibi corpus but doesn't implement the full set-of-scopes algorithm:
- Identifiers don't carry SET of scopes — just one env pointer
- Macro-generates-macro-generates-macro chains may have unintended captures we haven't tested
- bound-identifier=? / free-identifier=? are not exposed to user code (R7RS-large §6.x and Racket's syntax-protect API)
- Recursive macro expansion at different scope depths may collapse marks

## When it matters
Advanced macro libraries: pattern matchers, monadic do-notation expanders, compile-time code generators that produce multiple new bindings.

## Suggested fix
Implement Flatt's "Bindings as Sets of Scopes" (POPL 2016) properly:
- Each identifier carries Set<ScopeId> (HashSet<u64>)
- Every binding form mints a fresh ScopeId and adds it to all idents introduced in that scope
- Macro expansion adds a fresh "macro-introduction" ScopeId to every template-introduced identifier
- Lookup matches the binding whose scope-set is the largest subset of the identifier's scope-set
- Expose bound-identifier=? / free-identifier=? per R7RS-large

title: Exception handling
description: R7RS exception system: raise raise-continuable with-exception-handler, guard form, error error-object? error-object-message error-object-irritants error-object-message read-error? file-error?. Integrate with dynamic-wind from the continuations bead.
notes:
Added R7RS-small exception handling (~250 lines in eval.rs/value.rs/builtins.rs + 9 tests).

Value additions:
- Value::ErrorObject(Rc<ErrorObject>) where ErrorObject { message, irritants, kind: ErrorKind }
- ErrorKind { User, Read, File } (Read/File tags reserved for I/O-originated errors)

Step / Frame additions:
- Step::Raise(Value, bool) — bool = 'continuable'
- Frame::ExceptionHandler { handler, env }
- Frame::ReRaise — emits Step::Raise(value, false) after a non-continuable handler returns
- Frame::RaiseAfter { continuable } — pending raise after the operand is evaluated
- Frame::InstallHandler { thunk_expr, env } — installs handler after it's evaluated, then calls thunk

Eval-loop dispatch on Step::Raise:
- Pop frames into a temp stack looking for ExceptionHandler
- For raise-continuable: re-push popped frames so handler's return value substitutes for the raise expression (lands at the raise position)
- For plain raise: discard popped frames and push ReRaise so handler's return is re-raised to next outer handler

Special forms:
- raise / raise-continuable: push RaiseAfter, eval operand
- with-exception-handler: push InstallHandler, eval handler first; on its return install ExceptionHandler and call (thunk)
- guard: desugars to call/cc + with-exception-handler + cond — the cond runs INSIDE the handler but R7RS-correctly because (raise var) in the else clause finds the NEXT outer handler (our handler is already popped when invoked)

Primitives:
- error-object?, error-object-message, error-object-irritants, read-error?, file-error?
- make-error-object (used by the bootstrap  procedure)
- error in Scheme bootstrap: (define (error msg . irritants) (raise (apply make-error-object msg irritants)))

EvalError gained a Raised(Value) variant for uncaught raises bubbling out of eval().

Tests cover:
- Uncaught raise bubbles to EvalError::Raised
- with-exception-handler + escape via call/cc (the idiomatic 'caught' pattern)
- raise-continuable substitutes the handler's return value (key R7RS distinction)
- guard catches matching clause
- guard with no match re-raises
- guard else clause
- guard normal return (no exception)
- error constructs and raises a proper ErrorObject
- error-object? predicate after guard catches

EvalError dropped its #[derive(Eq, PartialEq)] because Value (now in the Raised variant) doesn't impl PartialEq.

title: call/cc and continuations
description: Implement first-class continuations: call-with-current-continuation (call/cc), dynamic-wind. R7RS requires full one-shot AND multi-shot continuations. Common approaches: CPS transform of the evaluator, or capture-the-stack via Rust generators / explicit continuation objects. Choose and document the approach. Verify with classic call/cc tests (generator patterns, escape continuations, coroutines).
notes:
Surfaced call/cc and the continuation infrastructure that was architecturally already in place from T7.

Changes:
- Added Value::Procedure::Continuation { frames: Vec<Frame> } variant
- Made Frame pub + #[derive(Clone)] so it can be cloned into the continuation value
- Added Step::InvokeContinuation(Vec<Frame>, Value) that the eval loop dispatches by replacing the live frame stack with the saved one and emitting Step::Return(value) — the exact semantics call/cc requires
- Added call/cc and call-with-current-continuation as special forms (step_call_cc). Captures frames.clone() BEFORE pushing its own CallOp so the continuation represents the call/cc-caller's pending work, not its own setup.
- step_apply handles Procedure::Continuation: takes args[0] (or Unspecified for 0 args) and emits InvokeContinuation.
- Added (apply proc a1 ... arglist) as a special form (step_apply_form) via a new Frame::ApplySpread variant that evaluates each operand in turn and spreads the last list before applying.
- Added dynamic-wind in the Scheme bootstrap: simple linear before/thunk/after sequencing (R7RS requires firing on continuation jumps in/out, which is documented as a v1 limitation).
- Refactored eval_source to evaluate all top-level datums inside a single (begin ...) wrapper, so continuations captured at top level can span across forms (R7RS semantics for the REPL/program top-level).

7 integration tests:
- call/cc with unused continuation
- escape continuation (classic 'jump out' pattern)
- continuation-as-value (saved, then invoked) — verifies the cross-form jump works
- call-with-current-continuation alias
- dynamic-wind sequence
- apply with arglist
- apply on user procedure

Documented v1 limitations:
- dynamic-wind doesn't intercept continuation jumps (R7RS §6.10's before/after-on-jump semantics)
- No multi-value continuations (defer to T-jee multi-values bead)
close_reason: call/cc, dynamic-wind, apply all working; 7 integration tests including cross-form continuation jump.

title: Performance: bytecode VM or AST compilation pass
description:
## Gap
ADR 0001 chose a tree-walking step-loop evaluator. The chibi corpus runs in ~230 ms total which is plenty fast for the test suite, but real workloads (tight inner loops in pure Scheme) will be 50-200x slower than a compiled implementation.

## When it matters
nscheme as a usable scripting tool, not just a teaching reference. Anything CPU-bound in pure Scheme.

## Suggested fix
Stage 1: precompile each lambda body to a flat IR at define time. Replace symbol-lookup with index-into-frame at compile time. ~3-5x speedup expected.

Stage 2: bytecode VM (stack-based, integer opcodes). Constants pool, jump tables. Tail-call as a single opcode. ~10-30x speedup expected.

Stage 3: profile-guided inlining of hot primitives. Optional.

Big project. Should be its own milestone, not a single bead. The ADR-0001 trade-off was deliberate; revisiting it requires its own ADR.

title: Delimited continuations (shift / reset) — not R7RS, but commonly expected
description:
## Gap
We implement R7RS \`call/cc\` (undelimited continuations). Many Scheme programs use the delimited family — \`reset\`, \`shift\`, \`call-with-prompt\` — for cleaner effect handling, generators, and async patterns. Not in R7RS-small.

## When it matters
Code ported from Racket / Chez / Guile that uses prompts. SRFI 226 (control features) standardises a Racket-flavoured API.

## Suggested fix
Implement \`call-with-prompt\` / \`abort-to-prompt\` plus \`reset\` / \`shift\` as derived forms. Our Frame stack architecture is friendly to this: a prompt is just a marker frame; abort truncates frames down to the marker.

Track SRFI 226 and align names if the SRFI is finalised.

title: Continuations retain frame storage indefinitely (no GC)
description:
## Gap
ADR 0004 noted: a captured continuation holds all the Frame storage that existed at capture time, alive via the Rc. We have no garbage collector — once a continuation is reachable (e.g., stored in a global), every closure / env / value transitively referenced stays alive forever.

## When it matters
Long-lived programs that capture continuations and then drop the reference. Web servers, REPLs, generators. Memory grows over time even though logically dead values are unreachable.

## Suggested fix
Two options, neither cheap:
1. Switch from Rc to a cycle-collecting GC (e.g., the \`gc\` crate, or a custom mark-and-sweep). Heavy refactor of Value.
2. Detect "shallow" continuations: most call/cc usage doesn't capture deeply, so we could trim the saved frame stack to just the active portion at capture time and rebuild on invoke. Doesn't help true escape continuations.

Acceptable workaround for now: document the limitation. The chibi tests don't exercise it.

Future-proofing nscheme as the spec stabilises.

## Suggested fix
Track http://r7rs.org / https://small.r7rs.org / https://docs.scheme.org/. When a docket is ratified, open a follow-up bead for that edition. Don't pre-implement WG drafts.

title: R7RS-large: Tangerine Edition (2019) libraries
description:
## Gap
R7RS-large Tangerine Edition (ratified 2019) adds these libraries on top of Red:

- (scheme bytevector)  — extra bytevector ops
- (scheme bitwise)     — SRFI 151 bitwise operations
- (scheme fixnum)      — SRFI 143 fixnum-specific arithmetic
- (scheme flonum)      — SRFI 144 flonum-specific arithmetic
- (scheme division)    — extended integer division
- (scheme fixnum)      — fixnum-only operators
- (scheme mapping)     — SRFI 146 functional maps
- (scheme mapping hash)— SRFI 146 hash-backed variant
- (scheme show)        — SRFI 159 formatting

## When it matters
Code that uses these (mostly newer SRFI-derived APIs).

## Suggested fix
Same approach as Red Edition (separate bead): port the SRFI reference implementations once the library loader supports it.

The fixnum / flonum libraries deserve attention: they assume the implementation distinguishes a tagged fixnum from a bignum. Our Value::Int / Value::BigInt split already does this — we'd need fxN-style operators that error on overflow instead of promoting (the R7RS-large semantics for fixnum ops).
notes: DESIGN (2026-06-02, approved): Phase 2 of R7RS-large after Red. Tangerine 9 libs as on-disk .scm. fixnum(143)/flonum(144) need fxN/flN operators (error-on-overflow for fixnum, leveraging existing Value::Int/BigInt split); bitwise(151) wants native bitwise primitives. division/bytevector are thin. mapping(146)+mapping-hash share core. show(159) is pure Scheme. One bead = one library = one commit, tests ported from each SRFI.
